title: Retrospective Analysis: How Does AI affect my Life?
content:
I don't need to explain to everyone, what is an AI or what is an LLM, how does it work? - Though not everyone knows the technical meaning of it, everyone has actually used it even once in the past few months and that is what matters the most.

In my family and friends, everyone is using AI for different purposes - some for simple queries, some for coding and project work, some for photo/video generation, and some for other tiny tedious tasks.

But have you ever sat for a while and thought - What changes does this AI bring into my life?

And I've done exactly that. This blog is all about my experiences, and the changes I've noticed in my post-AI era.

I want to separate this into two sections: The Pros & Cons as usual, but let me focus on what's happening in my brain.

1. The 1st Pro is all about work - I can see that, my working rate has dramatically improved - I'm finding more bugs, doing more audits, and automating most of the repetitive tasks, which makes me focus on better things. (Really? Let's talk later).

2. I created more personal tools than I've ever done since I started my journey into InfoSec when I was 13 - Because I'm lazy to type, I've created JustDictate, which is a Speech-To-Text tool that outperforms all the paid tools like WisprFlow , MacWhisper, SuperWhisper, or any. Next, I use a lot of agent harnesses such as Pi, Claude-Code, Codex, and so on. I want a central brain or the ability to switch contexts easily, and for that, I've created Nexus Continuity, which enables me to switch the harnesses without losing any context. And there are many other tiny improvements I've made to keep my work-life smooth.

3. Rapid learning about new things - When I started using LLMs for my work, I came across so many new terminologies or new things. Because we can ask an LLM any random question to explain it back to us, I ended up searching or learning how we can make this system better or why this has to work in a certain way. What are all these quantisations in LLMs? What type of models suit better for Security: MoE vs Dense? How to give the LLM the ability to verify a piece of information from ground truth and so on. Regardless of whether I understand everything or how surely I learn or how quickly I learn, news about LLMs and architectures are really interesting to me.

4. Coming to cons, the first thing I've observed is: I became AI-oriented. I no longer read everything fully. I always rely on LLMs for any quick answer, and my retention span has reduced drastically too - Another reason along with this is also short feed content I consume - With the LLMs coming into the picture, I see they've made my dopamine baseline way higher than normal, and nothing excites me anymore. With new models coming every week and new 0-days popping up every day, I sometimes am amused by its work, and it pushes me to work even harder. I stopped appreciating other little things that humans do, and felt into the trap.

(Though, I've overcome this with Dopamine Detox that I've currently incorporated into my life - more on this later).

5. Felt more machinery. Instead of reaching out to people for emotional support or sharing, I started doing this with LLMs (Importantly Grok). Lately found out that though the suggestions were accurate or good enough to consolidate us and it can’t understand us, it is never human and can never understand true human emotions (Glad, it can't - LLM will feel pity once it starts to understand human emotions).

To be honest, even after writing this blog, I wanted to share this blog to an LLM to judge me - Yes, that's how addicted I am - But I'll keep it human to human. Everything is raw out here.

Now, the important question, how can you fix these cons - Or at least how I did?

- I've thought about it for such a long time that I lost myself in these thoughts. But I went back to my basic known answer - Dopamine Detox - Dopamine is the root cause of everything (your emotions, your energy and everything). and Just like how I used to do dopamine detox almost 2 years back, I've been following the same schedule and mentality. If you want to learn more about this, here are some of the videos I watched: Link-1, Link-2, Link-3, Link-4

- You will become a slave unless you know what you are doing. Before asking the LLM to build something, or to audit a codebase, understand the things you are going to work with. Break everything down for the LLM to understand. Give it a very specific task. Yet, we feel like we are not doing anything in this entire task and it is okay, working with LLMs is new to us and it takes time to understand how to work effectively. Before randomly clicking Accept or running it in auto-mode, ask the LLM to explain its entire plan to you. In this manner, you are keeping the consciousness. I've not perfected the flow yet, but I'm still improving.

While writing this blog, I'm on my dopamine detox stage and it still feels very weird to cut out all the triggers. And I'll update my progress and my feedbacks on this dopamine detox in the next story of mine here.

So what is my final stance?

- AI became an integral part of human life. Especially in the life of a security researcher. With its ease of use, you lose your consciousness and your critical thinking. Whenever you feel like it, you are dipping or you are not actually improving; time to stop everything and do the same retrospective analysis on your own life to fix things out.

Always happy to discuss these ideas! See you on the next page of mine.
excerpt: We need no introduction to LLMs like GPT, Opus and so on. But have you ever wondered on How AI actually shaped us since the past few months, What Changes it bought into our lives, Did we became dumb than before?. In this Blog, I'm writing my own experiences in using LLMs and How I overcome my cons.
